title: Designing Flexible Data Infrastructure with Shared Semantics - NIEM, Ontologies & Knowledge Graphs
description:
Public data infrastructure is hard to modernise. Systems are fragmented across institutions, processes run on rigid rules, and much of the complexity was there for good reasons once.

At CDL26, Bradley Bolliger of EY shows how knowledge graphs can help institutions share data without forcing them onto a single system. This approach combines three things:
Entity-resolved knowledge graphs used as an operational data store
Shared semantics documented across separate institutions, using NIEM and formal ontologies
A collaborative knowledge base that records how its own definitions drift over time

Bradley will also cover how to use knowledge graphs as a design aid: mapping a problem space, aligning information flows to business needs, and building entity-centric data models that grow as each participant is ready.

This updated talk includes a worked example of shared semantics in practice, and the openings it creates for AI-enabled design and development.
